Description

Two proteins of the Golgi membrane hold parts of the cascade there. Sef binds active MEK, prevents the MEK:ERK complex from dissociating and blocks the nuclear translocation of active ERK. ERK held by Sef still phosphorylates RSK2 in the cytoplasm but no longer phosphorylates the nuclear transcription factor Elk-1, so Sef directs the signal to cytoplasmic targets [1]. RKTG (PAQR3) binds RAF1 and moves it from the cytoplasm to the Golgi. This blocks the move of RAF1 to the plasma membrane after EGF and reduces its interaction with RAS and MEK1 [2].

References

  1. Torii S, Kusakabe M, Yamamoto T, Maekawa M, Nishida E. Sef is a spatial regulator for Ras/MAP kinase signaling. Dev Cell. 2004;7(1):33-44. PMID: 15239952. doi: 10.1016/j.devcel.2004.05.019.
  2. Feng L, Xie X, Ding Q, Luo X, He J, Fan F, et al. Spatial regulation of Raf kinase signaling by RKTG. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2007;104(36):14348-53. PMID: 17724343. doi: 10.1073/pnas.0701298104.
